title: Why Does Lord Jagannath Have No Hands? The Legend of the Locked Door
description:
Manima! A king, a sacred log from the sea, and a carpenter who asked for one thing: never open the door.
The old legend of King Indradyumna and why Lord Jagannath of Puri has no hands. Jai Jagannath.
sources: Skanda Purana, Utkala Khanda (Purushottama Kshetra Mahatmya): legend of King Indradyumna
Odisha Review (Govt. of Odisha), June-July 2007: the Jagannath legend

scenes.label: Puri, Odisha
scenes.narration: The king threw open the door. The carpenter was gone, and the idols had no hands.
Three unfinished idols stared back, with great round eyes.

scenes.question: Why does Jagannath have no hands?
scenes.narration: So why is Jagannath, a form of Krishna, worshipped without hands?

scenes.label: Long, long ago
scenes.narration: Legend says King Indradyumna longed to build a great temple for Vishnu.
In a dream, he was told a sacred log would float in from the sea.
But no carpenter could carve it. Their tools simply broke.
Then a mysterious old carpenter arrived, with one rule.

scenes.label: 21 days
scenes.narration: Lock me in for twenty one days. Never open the door.
But before the days were up, the carving stopped. The queen feared he had died.
The king was heartbroken. Legend says the carpenter was Vishwakarma, the divine builder.
Then a divine voice said: worship the Lord just as he is.

scenes.label: Rath Yatra
scenes.narration: So to this day, Jagannath has no hands, and every year he rides out on his giant chariot.
Jai Jagannath. Follow for more stories like this.

topic: Why does Lord Jagannath have no hands? Tell the legend of King Indradyumna and the sculptor, as a story. Never draw the deity; show the king, the closed door and the temple.
